Use varargs for Ui messages and multi-keyword find
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui's private print helper now takes String... lines instead of a
single String, so multi-line messages (task added, marked, deleted)
no longer need manual "\n" concatenation. Existing single-string
calls are unaffected since Java wraps a lone argument into a
one-element array automatically.

TaskList.find and Parser.parseFindKeywords now take/return varargs
String[] arguments, so "find <keyword>" can search on multiple
space-separated keywords at once (e.g. "find book magazine" matches
tasks containing either word), returning their union with no
duplicates. Single-keyword find behaves exactly as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Varargs'
Improve naming per code quality guidelines
commitResults.messageBody:
Rename ToDos/Deadlines/Events to singular Todo/Deadline/Event (classes
should be nouns for one instance, not a collection). Rename
TaskList.getAll() to getAllTasks() so the name explains what it
returns. Rename the local variable holding a parsed task number to
zeroBasedIndex in Alice.getResponse, since that's the exact point
where the 1-based number the user typed gets converted to Java's
0-based indexing.

No behavior change: existing JUnit tests pass, and CLI/GUI were
manually re-verified.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Add assert statements to check preconditions that should always hold
if the rest of the code is correct: non-null/non-blank constructor
arguments, index bounds before array access, and non-empty varargs.
These are internal sanity checks, not user-input validation, so they
stay off by default and are enabled only for local runs via
enableAssertions in build.gradle.

commitResults.messageBody:
Pull out saveAndRespond() and parseValidIndex() in Alice, and
parseDateTime() in Parser, to remove the same few lines that were

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams API in TaskList.find and Storage.save
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the manual loops in find() and save() with a stream
filter/collect and map/join respectively, where the transformation is
a natural fit. Left the loops in Ui and Storage.load alone, since
their per-item indexing and per-line error handling don't translate
cleanly to a stream pipeline.

Handle command errors instead of crashing or ignoring them
commitResults.messageBody:
Alice previously stored any unrecognised input as a task, which turned
every typo into clutter and hid mistakes such as "mark" typed without a
task number. Malformed event commands were worse: writing /to before
/from threw an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException that terminated the text
UI. Storage failures were reported only to the console, which the GUI
never shows, so a failed save looked identical to a successful one.

Reject unknown commands with a message naming the valid ones, and give
each command taking a task number its own message when that number is
missing or non-numeric. Locate event markers by index rather than by
splitting, so a malformed command is reported rather than crashing, and
reject events that end before they start.

Introduce Response, which pairs a reply with whether it reports a
failure, so the GUI can style errors distinctly and a failed save is no
longer announced as a success.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreErrorHandling'
Show the task list live alongside the conversation
commitResults.messageBody:
Seeing what was on the list required typing "list" and reading a reply
that then scrolled away, so the actual state of the task list was never
visible for more than a moment.

Add a panel beside the conversation that redraws after every command,
showing each task's number, description, type and dates, with completed
tasks struck through. The panel hides itself when the window is too
narrow for two columns, and Alice exposes the tasks as an unmodifiable
list so a view cannot mutate them.

Rather than have the panel observe the task list, it re-reads it after
each command: TaskList is shared with the text UI and should not depend
on JavaFX. Each task also reports its own type name and schedule
summary, so the panel needs no instanceof checks.

Give Alice a distinct voice and a new avatar
commitResults.messageBody:
The replies were written in a generic assistant register that said
nothing about who Alice is, and the placeholder avatar was a plain
coloured glyph.

Rewrite every reply in a reluctant, faintly exasperated voice with a
matching face symbol, and replace the avatar with a cropped portrait
shown at 32px, since the previous 26px was too small to read as a
character. The attitude is confined to the framing: task numbers,
counts, dates and the cause of an error are all still stated plainly,
so a failed command is no harder to act on than before.

Face symbols are named constants written as Unicode escapes, which
keeps this file pure ASCII and so identical under any source encoding.

Broaden the test suite and fix what it exposed
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage had no tests at all despite being the component whose bugs cost
the user their data rather than merely confusing them, and TaskList.find
was untested despite being the most intricate method in the class.

Add StorageTest, UiTest, EventTest and TodoTest, and extend the existing
suites, taking the count from 48 to 105. UiTest in particular pins down
the rule that Alice's personality is only framing: it asserts that the
cause of an error survives into the message word for word.

Checking the new tests by deliberately breaking the code found two
things they could not catch. Deadline had no persistence tests, now
added. Task.toFileFormat turned out to be unreachable, since every
subclass overrides it and nothing has constructed a bare Task since
unrecognised input stopped being stored as one, so Task is now abstract
and declares it abstract instead.

The suite also exposed a portability bug: the day period was formatted
in the default locale, so the same deadline read "6:00 PM" under en but
"6:00 pm" under en-SG, and the CI job would have produced different
output on each of its three platforms. The formatters now pin
Locale.ENGLISH.
